info.name: Booking Microservices (Day 45)
info.description:
Local API collection for the booking learning project.

Progress covered:
- Day 9–15: flights CRUD, auth, audit, migrations
- Day 26–29: bookings, cancel, correlationId
- Day 31–34: Identity JWT + role; POST /api/flights requires admin JWT
- Day 35–40: api + identity run on Postgres (booking_db / identity_db); /ready checks Postgres

Import together with Booking-microservices.local.postman_environment.json.
Services: api http://localhost:3000, identity http://localhost:3001.
Flow: register -> promote-to-admin (CLI) -> login (sets accessToken, role=admin) -> create flight -> booking.
- Day 44: booking ownership — JWT on every booking route, GET /api/bookings(/:id), BOLA folder
- Day 45: airports + aircraft with seat layouts (reference data folder)

item.name: Flights (Write)
item.description:
Protected write endpoint. Requires Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}} with role=admin (Day 34).
Missing/invalid token -> 401; valid token but role != admin -> 403 FORBIDDEN.
Day 29: x-request-id becomes correlationId on flight.created outbox + flight_created_consumed logs.

item.name: Bookings
item.description:
Day 44: every booking route needs a JWT. Create/cancel need role=user (admins get 403); the booking's owner is the token's sub. Another account's booking answers 404 exactly like a missing one.
Run Identity → login bob first (saves userAccessToken). Day 29: x-request-id -> correlationId on booking.created.

item.name: Day 44 — Booking ownership (BOLA)
item.description:
Prerequisites: login bob (userAccessToken) and carol (userBAccessToken), an admin accessToken, create a flight, then POST a booking as bob (saves bookingId).
Every request below must be refused without revealing whether bob's booking exists.

request.description: Same 404 body as an unknown id (BR-AUTH-02).
Bob's booking stays active. Also 404 (never 409) after bob has cancelled it.

item.name: GET /api/bookings as carol → none of bob's

request.description: Only carol's own bookings.
Admins read every booking (BR-AUTH-03).
Admins do not book on someone's behalf (BR-AUTH-03).
Admins cancel only through flight cancellation.
Every booking route requires a JWT.

item.name: Day 45 — Reference data (airports, aircraft)
item.description:
Writes need an admin accessToken; GET /api/airports is public.
Optional: `npm run seed:reference --workspace=@booking-flight-system/api` adds 25 airports and 8 aircraft (idempotent).
The first two requests expect a fresh database: CXR / VN-A322 answer 409 on a second run.

request.description: US-REF-01. The code is upper-cased before saving. No Location header (no GET-by-code route).
BR-REF-04: an IANA name, never an offset like +07:00.
US-REF-03. Ordered by code, same pagination as flights.
US-REF-02. Answers seat counts per fare class, not the expanded seats.

exec: pm.test('38 seats: 8 business, 30 economy', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().seatsByFareClass).to.eql({ ECONOMY: 30, BUSINESS: 8 }));

request.description: BR-REF-06: limits are checked before any seat is generated (input amplification).
Day 45: a malformed id is 404, no longer a Postgres 500.

item.name: Identity (Day 31–34)
item.description:
Identity service on {{identityBaseUrl}} (default :3001), backed by identity_db (Postgres).
Register + JWT login. api verifies the JWT (shared JWT_SECRET) and POST /api/flights needs role=admin.
New users are role=user; promote with:
npm run promote-to-admin --workspace=@booking-flight-system/identity -- alice@example.com
then log in again to get a token with role=admin.

request.description: Identity liveness. 200 { status: ok }.

201 + { id, email, createdAt } — never passwordHash.
409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED on duplicate.
422 validation (email format, password >= 8).
Run after a successful register with the same email. Expect 409.

200 + { accessToken, expiresIn }. Payload is { sub, email, role } — readable without JWT_SECRET (signed, not encrypted).
Paste accessToken into jwt.io to verify.
Saves accessToken to environment on success. Promote user to admin before creating flights.
401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS — same message as unknown email (no user enumeration).
401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS — identical body to wrong-password case.
Expect 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.
Second account that stays role=user (do NOT promote). Used to demo 403 on POST /api/flights.
Saves userAccessToken (role=user) to the environment.
Day 44: a second role=user account, used to show one user cannot see or cancel another's booking.
Saves userBAccessToken (role=user).
